title: Minimax Precision for the Utility of Surrogate-Ranked Capacity-Constrained Treatment Policies
banked_reason: D0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: tier subfield < field; NOT salvageable in scope, projected paper-score ceiling 6.5 < 7.4. Mathematical referee passed; editorial ballast remains unrepaired.
gap_reasons: The delivered sharp comparison is confined to a known-uniform, two-feature, half-capacity model with fixed smoothness and small affine contrast neighborhoods.
The matching and strict-penalty claims are supported within the specified model, but the narrow scope and absence of useful finite-sample calibration constrain the leading-journal paper score.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 produced matching original-record observational n^(-6/31) and fair-assignment n^(-3/7) risk and honest-length claims, with n^(51/217) confounding penalty; the mathematical referee passed with no findings. Novelty was capped at subfield against the mandatory field floor, with paper-score ceiling 6.5 below 7.4 and no bounded improvement in scope. Three editorial ballast findings remain unrepaired; confidence calibration is uninformative at feasible sample sizes, and no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: The causal primary utility of a half-capacity surrogate-ranked treatment policy has sharp original-record absolute-risk and exactly finite \(90\%\)-honest connected-interval length orders \(n^{-6/31}\) with unknown rough confounding and \(n^{-3/7}\) with supplied fair assignment. Both results hold on the unchanged known-uniform binary parents, with two unknown \(C^3\) causal contrasts, a learned population median and primary boundary utility, and arbitrary conditional endpoint correlation. Total computable finite projection rules, public error budgets and full-range fallbacks attain these orders; normalized compatible original Bernoulli likelihoods give all-procedure converses. Unknown confounding incurs a strict precision penalty of order \(n^{51/217}\), and risk and honest expected interval length have the same order on each parent.
gap: Xu and coauthors's surrogate-efficiency remainder theorem and Chen and Gao's direct-regression contour theorem do not determine this original-record benchmark's minimax precision or exactly finite-honest interval length. The closer internal sign-share donor treats a different scalar and supplies informal method architecture, not this theorem.
fill: The frontier question requires computable full-parent attainers, evaluated numerical and statistical budgets, and same-parent normalized original likelihoods. Unknown utility and the learned exact-capacity cutoff remain first-class parts of both the upper transfer and scalar lower separation.
